lessons.title: eleven to twenty
lessons.lesson:
New: eleven-fifteen, sixteen-twenty (chant-carried in two groups of five, like Grade 1)

Presentation: teen chant 11-15, then 16-20; each number = numeral + a TALLY BUNDLE (one bundle
of ten + extras - place-value seeded without naming it): "Ten... and one more... eleven!" Tudlo Guide stacks
lily pads: a raft of ten plus loose ones.
(Hiligaynon note: everyday speech uses Spanish-derived forms - onse, dose, trese, katorse, kinse,
disesais, disesiete, disiocho, disinueve, bainte. CONFIRM exact local forms/spellings with your
validators; your panel may prefer native forms in the docs.) (Maam Alog corrected numbering:
napulo kag isa (11), napulo kag duha (12), napulo kag tatlo (13), napulo kag apat (14), napulo kag
lima (15), napulo kag anum (16), napulo kag pito (17), napulo kag walo (18), napulo kag siyam (19),
and duha ka napulo (20).)

UNIT 3 - FABLES
UNIT 3 - FABLES (Sugilanon nga may Leksyon) -
3 lessons
Short retold fables (public domain: one Philippine folktale + two Aesop) in the appâ€™s OWN simple
words - 8 short sentences max, 4 pages, question every 1-2 pages. New skill: the MORAL - what the
story teaches, not just what happens (the first step from literal to inferential comprehension). Tudlo Guide
hosts each fable and reacts to it.
Each fable pre-teaches its 3-4 new words Grade-1-style (image + audio + word, 90 seconds) BEFORE
the story - the standard comprehension scaffold.
Unit 3 asset list: 12 fable-page illustrations, 5 fable-animal characters, moral-choice card UI,
prediction-page UI (guess saved + revisited), pre-teach word cards, per-sentence audio.

lessons.title: â€œThe Monkey and the Turtleâ€ (Philippine folktale)
lessons.story:
Pre-story words: monkey (amo) Â· turtle (bao) Â· banana tree Â· share
FULL RETOLD TEXT (8 short sentences, 4 pages):
â— Page 1: "Turtle finds a banana tree in the river. Monkey says, 'Let's share!'"
â— Q1 - WHO: "Who finds the tree?" â†’ tap Turtle
â— Page 2: "'I take the top!' says Monkey. Turtle takes the bottom."
â— Q2 - WHAT: "What does Monkey take?" â†’ tap the leafy top (vs roots)
â— Page 3: "Monkey's top dies. Turtle's bottom grows tall!"
â— Q3 - WHY (the first WHY!): "Why does Turtle's part grow?" â†’ tap the roots picture (vs
leaves) - Tudlo Guide whispers the hint if retried: "Ang gamot ang nagakuha sang tubig!"
â— Page 4: "Now Turtle has many bananas. He shares them with his friends anyway!"
â— MORAL PAGE: Tudlo Guide asks: "Ano ang leksyon?" â†’ 2 spoken+written choices: "Share fairly." vs
"Bananas are yummy." (one real moral, one silly-literal - teaches the CATEGORY of moral by
contrast)
After-story: TileBuilder: "Turtle shares + his bananas" Â· voice-read Turtle's kind line.

UNIT 4 - STORY DETECTIVES
UNIT 4 - STORY DETECTIVES (Reading
Comprehension) - 3 lessons
Comprehension STRATEGIES trained explicitly, disguised as detective work: Detective Tudlo Guide gets a hat
and a magnifying glass; every question type is a detective tool. Content = micro-mysteries of 4-6 short
sentences (attention-span friendly), built entirely from known words - the skills are the curriculum.
Unit 4 asset list: detective Tudlo Guide art (hat + glass), footprint-trail UI, crystal-ball UI, Goldilocks card UI
(too small / wrong / just right), 10 micro-mystery illustration sets, question bank (4-6 extra questions
per Unit 2-3 story for detective mode).

Presentation: Detective Tudlo Guide models on a 4-sentence micro-mystery, thinking ALOUD:
"The plate is empty! The fish is gone. Look - paw prints! The cat sleeps with a happy

â— Q: "WHAT is the problem?" â†’ wet floor Â· Q: "WHY is the floor wet?" â†’ rain through the
window, TAP THE CLUE â†’ "The window is open." Â· Q: "Was it Bantay?" â†’ No, TAP THE CLUE
â†’ "Bantay is dry."
Mystery C - "Ang Nagahibi nga Bata" (The Crying Baby):

SEQUENCING HALF - signal words first, next, then, last taught with a 4-step visual routine (planting:
"First dig. Next, the seed. Then, water. Last - a flower!"). Practice: 3 scrambled picture-stories
(getting dressed / cooking rice / Tudlo Guide's morning) â†’ drag into order along the footprint trail. Then
ONE TEXT-ONLY sequencing (4 short sentences, no pictures - the app's first pictureless
comprehension, the real milestone):
"First, Tudlo Guide wakes up. Next, she eats. Then, she hops to school. Last, she reads a book."
(shuffled â†’ order)
PREDICTING HALF - the crystal ball: stories stop before the ending; the child guesses. FULL TEXTS:
1. "The sky is dark. Nanay takes the laundry inside. What happens NEXT?" â†’ 3 picture choices
(rain / fiesta / turtle) â†’ rain
2. "Bantay smells food. He runs to the kitchen. What happens NEXT?" â†’ (he begs for food / he
sleeps / he swims)
3. "Ana plants a seed. She waters it every day. What happens NEXT?" â†’ (a flower grows / it
snows / a bus comes) EITHER right or wrong, Tudlo Guide celebrates the ACT of predicting
("Detective guess!") and shows the clue that pointed to the answer.

lessons.title: Context Clues + THE GRADE 3 / APP CAPSTONE
lessons.lesson:
CONTEXT CLUES (the graduation skill): Tudlo Guide meets 4 sentences, each with one unknown word; the
surrounding sentence gives the meaning away. Pattern per item: READ â†’ GUESS from 3 picture
choices â†’ the CLUE WORDS light up â†’ confirm. FULL TEXTS:
1. "Bantay is very gutom - he eats and eats and eats!" â†’ gutom = ? â†’ hungry (clues: "eats and
eats")
2. "The night is very madulom - Tudlo Guide cannot see!" â†’ dark (clue: "cannot see")
3. "Lola's soup is mainit - be careful, do not touch!" â†’ hot (clues: "careful... do not touch")
4. "Juan is kapoy - he ran twenty laps! He wants to sleep." â†’ tired (clues: "ran... wants to
sleep")
(Design note: the mystery words are HILIGAYNON words embedded in English sentences - the child
decodes meaning from ENGLISH context, then Tudlo Guide reveals the English word. This flips the app's usual
direction and mirrors real bilingual reading. If validators prefer invented words instead, swap them in
- the mechanic is unchanged.)
Tudlo Guide then says the line that is the whole app in one sentence: "Kon indi mo kilala ang word - BASAHA
ANG PALIBOT NIYA!" (If you don't know the word - read around it!)
THE GRADE 3 / APP CAPSTONE - "Ang Graduation ni Tudlo Guide!" A final SHORT story (8 sentences -
attention-span capped) told in stops across the whole map, with ~14 embedded items sampling
every Grade 3 skill. FULL STORY TEXT:
â— Page 1: "Today is a big day. Tudlo Guide graduates!" â†’ 2 number items: "How many friends come?"
(count 12) Â· "How much are the flowers?" (price tag: 15 pesos)
â— Page 2: "First, the friends make the plaza pretty. Ana brings long green leaves. Juan brings
round red lanterns." â†’ 2 describing taps + 1 sequence item (first/next/then cards)
â— Page 3: "But the sky is dark! What happens next?" â†’ 1 prediction (rain!) â†’ "Teacher says:
'To the school!'" â†’ 1 WH + evidence tap: "Why do they move?" â†’ tap the clue sentence
â— Page 4: "Lolo tells one last riddle. Lola reads one small poem." â†’ 1 riddle (Grade 2 pouch,
scheduler-picked) + 1 rhyme-completion
â— Page 5: "Tudlo Guide says: 'Salamat - THANK YOU, my friends!' Everyone is happy - not sad!" â†’ 1
opposite tap + 1 context-clue word + 1 main-idea card ("Friends help each other" - just right!)
â— FINALE: the child voice-reads the last line aloud: "Goodbye, and thank you!" (record â†’
playback â†’ the whole map cheers)
First-attempt data here = the terminal assessment; with the Grade 1 and Grade 2 capstones you now
have THREE comparable instruments charting the entire learning arc (the spine of your evaluation
chapter).
